scope: 57 individually judged members; three existing archive convictions retained. Debian extraction roots omit the archive data/ prefix.
provenance_and_missing_context: Kali/Empire/DAVTest packaging supports authorized testing as an alternative explanation. Each selected member is a functional attack implementation, not merely documentation or an ordinary vendored support library. Credential/identity abuse, exploit execution, covert surveillance, unauthenticated command access or implant tasking tips the individual MALICIOUS judgments. No target authorization, deployment history or successful execution is supplied. Unconfigured payload templates are identified as templates, without inventing endpoints or final payloads.
method: Ran atomscan in slow mode with dependency following disabled and cleave facts for every member and archive.

Read source control/data paths, decoded Base64/gzip/deflate/native payloads, inspected managed IL with dnfile/dncil and native code with rizin. Independently recovered the macOS evolving-XOR AppleScript. No sample code was executed.
Re-ran all 60 scans and compared every analyzed member/layer, normalizing only the intentional rule-ID relocation.
Repeated macOS member/archive scans uncached to investigate native extractor variation.

change.reason: Run-key login activation belongs under login/registry/run-key, rather than login/startup/registry.
change.matcher_scope_criticality_confidence_and: Byte-for-byte unchanged YAML contents; relocation only.
change.consumer_audit: No exact YAML consumers or differing old-ancestor selectors exist. The two new run-key directory consumers are Go/binary-only and cannot consume the moved PowerShell-only rule. Broader persistence/login selectors retain membership. Historical scan/review JSON keeps its recorded old IDs.
change.positive: Invoke-PrintDemon.ps1: all three legs, file scope and two-line proximity still match.

detection_comparison.powershell_and_davtest_findings: Exactly retained after normalizing the relocated ID, including archive-member findings.
detection_comparison.macos_native_variation: Unchanged Mach-O bytes produced differing native extraction/merge results: the standalone after scan has 28 fewer lower-tier IDs and two new IDs, including x64-vs-ARM64 XOR mechanism attribution. Lower-tier changes include redundant HTTP/unzip/process/target-path facts, compiler/hardening metadata and a UUID fact. Four hostile and three suspicious detections remain unchanged. An uncached standalone repeat reproduced the after findings/probability; the uncached archive repeat switched the XOR attribution back, confirming run variation independent of this PowerShell-only relocation. Do not infer that a native behavior is absent from a missing lower-tier finding.
detection_comparison.classifier_disagreement: All 57 members judged MALICIOUS; classifier retains benign/suspicious gates for the listed members despite supported hostile detections. No duplicate rules or score-driven severity edits added.
engine_limitations: Atomscan logs report model feature-spec v18 versus extractor v19.
PHP member reports flow-call-unavailable; its request-to-system and file-management flow is explicit in source.

members_and_archives.marker_note: WireTap: keylogs and records audio, camera and screenshots
members_and_archives.analysis: Base64 -> gzip -> Assembly.Load -> WireT4p.Program.main. IL resolves speech recognition to credential-word-triggered audio recording, keyboard callbacks to trace output, desktop and DirectShow frame capture to saved images; clipboard monitoring also logs content.
members_and_archives.coverage_note: Existing hostile findings describe the supported attack behavior; accurate neutral capabilities are retained.

members_and_archives.marker_note: Mimikatz: reflective LSASS and protected private-key extraction
members_and_archives.analysis: The x64 and x86 embedded native images export powershell_reflective_mimikatz. The wrapper selects sekurlsa::logonpasswords or CAPI/CNG export-protection patching and certificate export, clears PE magic, manually maps the image and invokes the export. Native memory-read call sites were inspected.
members_and_archives.coverage_note: Existing hostile findings describe the supported attack behavior; accurate neutral capabilities are retained.

members_and_archives.marker_note: BypassUAC: injected DLL hijack with self-deleting batch launcher
members_and_archives.analysis: Writes a command batch and DLL payload, patches architecture-specific loader data, injects into hidden notepad, and prepares CRYPTBASE/sysprep or NTWDBLIB/cliconfg hijacking. The native DLL export builds cmd.exe /C and calls CreateProcessA. The batch deletes itself.
members_and_archives.coverage_note: Existing hostile findings describe the supported attack behavior; accurate neutral capabilities are retained.

members_and_archives.marker_note: DCSync: reflectively invokes domain password-hash replication
members_and_archives.analysis: Manually maps the embedded Mimikatz images, invokes the native command export with lsadump::dcsync /user, and parses returned RID/NTLM hash fields. Domain replication privileges remain prerequisites.
members_and_archives.coverage_note: The two hostile identity rules describe the same DCSync replication payload at different implementation layers. Reflective mapping remains separately covered as a capability; no additional credential source is invented.

members_and_archives.marker_note: PowerBreach: remote script evaluation with network activation triggers
members_and_archives.analysis: Invoke-CallbackIEX downloads or BITS-stages a resource, Base64-decodes it and evaluates the decoded script. Callback loops retry it; DNS, Security-event and packet-knock paths activate callbacks. A helper opens broad PowerShell firewall rules.
members_and_archives.coverage_note: Existing hostile findings describe the supported attack behavior; accurate neutral capabilities are retained.

members_and_archives.marker_note: SweetPotato: coerces privileged tokens and executes commands
members_and_archives.analysis: Base64 assembly is loaded and SweetPotato.Program.main receives executable, arguments, listener and exploit options. IL dispatches COM/NTLM, print or EFS impersonation paths, obtains a privileged token and calls CreateProcessWithTokenW/CreateProcessAsUserW.
members_and_archives.coverage_note: The two hostile identity rules describe wrapper and compiled forms of one privilege-impersonation exploit. Native code implements several coercion variants; this is not counted as unrelated attack objectives.

members_and_archives.analysis: Gzip-decoded managed payload is loaded and invoked. DoStuff saves remote SAM and SECURITY hives to ADMIN$ paths, retrieves them, derives boot keys, calls ParseSam/ParseLsa to decrypt secrets and removes dump files.
members_and_archives.coverage_note: Existing hostile findings describe the supported attack behavior; accurate neutral capabilities are retained.

members_and_archives.marker_note: MS16-032: leaked-handle token race executes a SYSTEM command
members_and_archives.analysis: Creates suspended logon processes with inherited thread handles, duplicates leaked handles, uses NtImpersonateThread to acquire SYSTEM tokens, then races SetThreadToken against CreateProcessWithLogonW and resumes a privileged child.
members_and_archives.coverage_note: Existing hostile findings describe the supported attack behavior; accurate neutral capabilities are retained.

members_and_archives.analysis: Architecture-specific VNC payloads are decoded, PE magic is cleared, and a reflective mapper invokes the native image with bind/reverse VNC parameters. The wrapper can target remote memory but also explicitly supports local image mapping. This is an embedded remote-control payload, not an ordinary VNC installer.

members_and_archives.analysis: Selects or clones Winlogon, reflectively injects the logon DLL, then writes domain/user/password/logon options to its named pipe. Native VoidFunc reads those bytes, calls LsaLogonUser and impersonates the resulting token. This relocates the credential logon into Winlogon.
